messages.content: Predict a person's decision in the combined ultimatum and dictator game. Each trial concerns a different real counterpart: received proposals were said to come from past participants, and the participant's proposals would be used with future participants. There are three roles. UG_PROPOSER (square cue): the participant has the displayed pot of 15–25 US dollars and chooses one of the two displayed dollar amounts to offer the counterpart, keeping the remainder if accepted. The counterpart may reject, making both get zero. DG_PROPOSER (triangle cue): choose one of the two dollar offers from the displayed pot; the recipient is passive and cannot reject, and the participant keeps the remainder. UG_RECIPIENT (circle cue): the other person has the displayed pot and offers the nonzero amount to the participant. Choose ACCEPT to receive that amount while the proposer gets the remainder, or REJECT to give both zero. The zero-valued screen option is the reject button, not a second proposal. Left and right sides change across trials. Button 2 selects LEFT and button 3 selects RIGHT; button 2 does not always reject. For a proposer the target is the selected number of US dollars offered to the recipient, NOT a key number, self payoff, percentage or MORE/LESS category. For a recipient the target is ACCEPT or REJECT. There is no arbitrary A/B coding and no free allocation outside the two displayed amounts. Both payoff possibilities are shown in the current options: self and other mean potential dollar payoffs if that option is implemented and, where relevant, accepted; they are not a realized payment or known counterpart reply. A decision has a nominal three-second response window. A recorded valid button near a display-frame boundary is retained; a missed response is not a rejection or zero-dollar offer. The screen confirms a selected option by color, or says that the trial was missed. It does not reveal a real acceptance by the counterpart or a cash payoff after each trial. Participants were told one proposal would be randomly selected at study end for a bonus depending on its outcome. This does not mean all offers are paid or every partner accepts. The amount or payment pool of other tasks is not supplied as this trial's stake. A square/triangle/circle merely denotes the explicitly described role; no human face is drawn in the supplied UGDG choice code. The current event gives the run and trial within this game, role, pot and two visible options. Earlier-event lines give strictly earlier trials of these two formal UGDG runs, including missed trials; their response is the earlier chosen dollar offer, ACCEPT/REJECT or MISSED. These are the same participant's past decisions with different counterparts, not repeated play with one partner. Past actual counterpart acceptance and realized payoffs remain unknown. No chronology or outcomes of other scanner tasks or practice are inferred. The profile gives self-reported age in years at the appointment, gender (Man/Woman), race, handedness (Left/Right), BMI if available, and the screening answer Yes/No to whether any medication was taken in the past month, if available. BMI and medication missingness is not filled. Medication use does not imply a diagnosis. Experimenter deception ratings, lab tests, unlabeled questionnaire items, current response/RT and future information are absent. Predict the recorded choice without an explanation. Current target: output only the selected offer in US dollars as an integer, with no currency sign.

Each trial concerns a different real counterpart: received proposals were said to come from past participants, and the participant's proposals would be used with future participants. There are three roles. UG_PROPOSER (square cue): the participant has the displayed pot of 15–25 US dollars and chooses one of the two displayed dollar amounts to offer the counterpart, keeping the remainder if accepted. The counterpart may reject, making both get zero. DG_PROPOSER (triangle cue): choose one of the two dollar offers from the displayed pot; the recipient is passive and cannot reject, and the participant keeps the remainder. UG_RECIPIENT (circle cue): the other person has the displayed pot and offers the nonzero amount to the participant. Choose ACCEPT to receive that amount while the proposer gets the remainder, or REJECT to give both zero. The zero-valued screen option is the reject button, not a second proposal. Left and right sides change across trials. Button 2 selects LEFT and button 3 selects RIGHT; button 2 does not always reject. For a proposer the target is the selected number of US dollars offered to the recipient, NOT a key number, self payoff, percentage or MORE/LESS category. For a recipient the target is ACCEPT or REJECT. There is no arbitrary A/B coding and no free allocation outside the two displayed amounts. Both payoff possibilities are shown in the current options: self and other mean potential dollar payoffs if that option is implemented and, where relevant, accepted; they are not a realized payment or known counterpart reply. A decision has a nominal three-second response window. A recorded valid button near a display-frame boundary is retained; a missed response is not a rejection or zero-dollar offer. The screen confirms a selected option by color, or says that the trial was missed. It does not reveal a real acceptance by the counterpart or a cash payoff after each trial. Participants were told one proposal would be randomly selected at study end for a bonus depending on its outcome. This does not mean all offers are paid or every partner accepts. The amount or payment pool of other tasks is not supplied as this trial's stake. A square/triangle/circle merely denotes the explicitly described role; no human face is drawn in the supplied UGDG choice code. The current event gives the run and trial within this game, role, pot and two visible options. Earlier-event lines give strictly earlier trials of these two formal UGDG runs, including missed trials; their response is the earlier chosen dollar offer, ACCEPT/REJECT or MISSED. These are the same participant's past decisions with different counterparts, not repeated play with one partner. Past actual counterpart acceptance and realized payoffs remain unknown. No chronology or outcomes of other scanner tasks or practice are inferred. The profile gives self-reported age in years at the appointment, gender (Man/Woman), race, handedness (Left/Right), BMI if available, and the screening answer Yes/No to whether any medication was taken in the past month, if available. BMI and medication missingness is not filled. Medication use does not imply a diagnosis. Experimenter deception ratings, lab tests, unlabeled questionnaire items, current response/RT and future information are absent. Predict the recorded choice without an explanation. Current target: output only the selected offer in US dollars as an integer, with no currency sign.

Each trial concerns a different real counterpart: received proposals were said to come from past participants, and the participant's proposals would be used with future participants. There are three roles. UG_PROPOSER (square cue): the participant has the displayed pot of 15–25 US dollars and chooses one of the two displayed dollar amounts to offer the counterpart, keeping the remainder if accepted. The counterpart may reject, making both get zero. DG_PROPOSER (triangle cue): choose one of the two dollar offers from the displayed pot; the recipient is passive and cannot reject, and the participant keeps the remainder. UG_RECIPIENT (circle cue): the other person has the displayed pot and offers the nonzero amount to the participant. Choose ACCEPT to receive that amount while the proposer gets the remainder, or REJECT to give both zero. The zero-valued screen option is the reject button, not a second proposal. Left and right sides change across trials. Button 2 selects LEFT and button 3 selects RIGHT; button 2 does not always reject. For a proposer the target is the selected number of US dollars offered to the recipient, NOT a key number, self payoff, percentage or MORE/LESS category. For a recipient the target is ACCEPT or REJECT. There is no arbitrary A/B coding and no free allocation outside the two displayed amounts. Both payoff possibilities are shown in the current options: self and other mean potential dollar payoffs if that option is implemented and, where relevant, accepted; they are not a realized payment or known counterpart reply. A decision has a nominal three-second response window. A recorded valid button near a display-frame boundary is retained; a missed response is not a rejection or zero-dollar offer. The screen confirms a selected option by color, or says that the trial was missed. It does not reveal a real acceptance by the counterpart or a cash payoff after each trial. Participants were told one proposal would be randomly selected at study end for a bonus depending on its outcome. This does not mean all offers are paid or every partner accepts. The amount or payment pool of other tasks is not supplied as this trial's stake. A square/triangle/circle merely denotes the explicitly described role; no human face is drawn in the supplied UGDG choice code. The current event gives the run and trial within this game, role, pot and two visible options. Earlier-event lines give strictly earlier trials of these two formal UGDG runs, including missed trials; their response is the earlier chosen dollar offer, ACCEPT/REJECT or MISSED. These are the same participant's past decisions with different counterparts, not repeated play with one partner. Past actual counterpart acceptance and realized payoffs remain unknown. No chronology or outcomes of other scanner tasks or practice are inferred. The profile gives self-reported age in years at the appointment, gender (Man/Woman), race, handedness (Left/Right), BMI if available, and the screening answer Yes/No to whether any medication was taken in the past month, if available. BMI and medication missingness is not filled. Medication use does not imply a diagnosis. Experimenter deception ratings, lab tests, unlabeled questionnaire items, current response/RT and future information are absent. Predict the recorded choice without an explanation. Current target: output only the selected offer in US dollars as an integer, with no currency sign.
